q: Which defence level are you actually facing?
why: Mapped to the defence scale in the ontology: F2 signature, F3 protocol aware, F4 in app, F5 bot management, F6 identity, F7 model based. Each needs a different approach and most of them need no payload at all.

branches.action: encoding and syntax mutation against the class, one axis at a time so you learn which axis is filtered
branches.oracle: payload passes where a control is blocked

branches.action: semantic bypass, not encoding. the parser difference between two layers is the opening
branches.oracle: two layers disagree about the same request

branches.action: differential test: same request from a plain client and a real browser profile. if the answers differ, the defence is the client
branches.oracle: response obtained only with a browser shaped client

branches.a: F7 model based or rate based
branches.action: pace deliberately and keep a request budget. the goal is a result inside the budget, not speed
stop and report it. solving that is out of scope for an assessment and is a business decision, not a technical one
